# GoFurry V0.1-D1-B2 — Site Yearbook Complete Closure Contract

**Status:** implementation-ready and scope-frozen, 2026-11-11.
**Target:** `librecosta/gofurry`, **develop** only.
**One-pass objective:** finish the public, automatically generated, traceable Site Yearbook **and** the associated long-term coverage compaction, without expanding into Tech Weekly or changing the carefully polished Start experience.

## 0. Baseline and course correction

- D1-A commit `577a230db5f814380d0884bcb565719b89d0dba3`: Site/Game UUIDv7 and 16-char Public ID, published locales, canonical SSR routes, Site addresses, Game sources.
- D1-B1 implementation `a0b89ddf7aa46a7753fd6fbe8a319aeb0f25ce57`, then CI fixes through `3764fb10d99c77b718be87cf346e1fe8da2a9e37`; GitHub Actions run `43030496801` succeeded.
- B1 acceptance at `docs/v0.1-d1-b1-acceptance.md`: `collection_sources`, bindings, plans, cursor, scoped current, `site_evidence_changes`, `site_daily_coverage`, Steam observations. Authenticated Harvest API and two independent PostgreSQL systems, 410 reset, old evidence preserved. B1 measured **~262 KB per Site-year** for one confirmed scope per day plus four transitions; multiple scopes grow that number. No public yearbook yet.
- B1 originally created numerous internal and cross-domain **foreign keys**, mostly RESTRICT/default NO ACTION; do not call them cascades. They require a deliberate simplification review according to the user's stated preference for **no FK/cascade except demonstrably high-value intra-aggregate cases**.
- The original ordering of yearbook before the core Site/Game UI was overly ambitious. Finish this already-started capability **now**, in one focused stage, then return directly to navigation/catalog, game UX, Admin and legacy migration. Do not reopen upstream Harvest or redesign Start.

READ: AGENTS.md, .agents/architecture.md, `docs/v0.1-d1-a-acceptance.md`, `docs/v0.1-d1-b-harvest-evidence-yearbook.md`, `docs/v0.1-d1-b1-acceptance.md`; real current Go/SQL in `services/api/internal/{collection,catalog,server}`, Go migrations/queries, TanStack Start `apps/web/src/catalog/detail.tsx`, public routes, cache/SEO localization rules. Harvest V0.1-D is **read-only reference**.

## 1. Product and release-completeness

Site Yearbook is **one per Site identity and UTC calendar year**, not per domain and not a global observations portal. It is a permanent, accessible, bilingual (zh/en) editorial-quality page based only on proved, sanitized recorded history. A domain migration must preserve Site identity and historical attribution.

The stage is complete only when ALL of the following exist:
1. Persisted, revisioned annual snapshots and explicit publication/visibility semantics.
2. Real deterministic generation with trustworthy evidence, idempotent UTC annual auto-run, manual safe preview/reconcile and no busy loop/new microservice.
3. Accurate completeness and coverage disclaimers, including unknown days, changing target/region, partial year and ruleset changes.
4. Public GoFurry **API + SSR page** at the reserved Yearbook URL with localized canonical and hreflang, 200/301/404/503 correctness, responsive light/dark presentation and Site detail entry.
5. No unbounded growth of raw daily coverage: implement, prove and measure **monthly coverage compaction** while preserving enough day-level evidence for yearbooks and later audit/revisions.
6. Schema minimization/FK and cascade audit, no damage to existing data, no regressions of Site/Game or Start.
7. An actually executed end-to-end acceptance; full CI must pass.

No tech-weekly publishing, PDF rendering, automated station-owner emailing, user-generated edits, AI-generated assertions, sitemap crawler, image-generation assets, new Admin redesign, generalized metrics/warehouse or multi-platform acquisition. Steam/Game yearbook is **out**.

## 2. Annual semantics and eligibility

- All periods UTC: year interval `[YYYY-01-01T00:00Z, (YYYY+1)-01-01T00:00Z)`. Report year `2026` is **not finalizable or publicly publishable on 2026-11-11**; the first automatic closure candidate is **2027-01-08 00:00 UTC** (7 calendar days grace after year end). Test earlier-year fixtures deterministically using an injected clock/test DB; no clock spoofing in production.
- Process **published, eligible, recorded** Site entities only for new automatic annual publications. An archived Site should not trigger new automatic public yearbooks. A **previously published yearbook is a distinct historical record** and may remain accessible after a Site is archived unless an explicit Yearbook visibility removal policy is applied. Never leak drafts, withdrawn pages, private reasons or previously unpublished observations.
- Default initial auditable eligibility policy: at least **14 distinct UTC dates** with verified Site coverage spread across a span of **28 calendar days or more**, and at least one valid, attributable compact baseline fact. Days may be nonconsecutive. These thresholds are a modest minimum **quality gate**, not a claim of full-year coverage or uptime. A Site recorded only 2 days gets `insufficient_evidence`, not a synthetic annual report. Design threshold implementation as a versioned fixed internal policy, NOT a maze of per-site runtime knobs.
- Repeated confirmed scopes on the same UTC day count as **one distinct Site day** for the eligibility threshold, not one day per capability/locale/egress. Ignore duplicate coverage, unsupported facts and dates outside effective binding periods. The first/last seen period and all observation gaps are shown; never count missing dates as outages.
- Distinguish `period_start/end` (calendar), `recorded_from/to` (actually covered), observed-day count, qualifying sources/capabilities, gap count/known gaps, and `partial_year` classification. A 2026 record first seen 2026-11-11 is **partial year**, even if there are many observations in Nov/Dec. Never backfill January–October.
- Year-end state uses the **last verifiable observation no later than the year cutoff** and carries its real last-observed timestamp and evidence confidence. A pre-year carry-forward fact is labeled prior-known with its original last-observed date, not recast as a fresh January reading.
- Source fact `first_observed_at` is *detection time*, not verified time of the real event or technology migration. Include detector ruleset/projection version and meaningful evidence signals. A fingerprint rule upgrade, change of observation vantage, inconclusive/non-detection or proxy/CDN presentation variation cannot by itself create a claimed platform migration.
- No % uptime, business ranking/security grade, “online all year”, “always reachable”, inferred exact upgrade date, invented site age, scraped owner contacts, annual historical Steam stats or unsupported date precision. Site Data observations are **not** an Uptime service.

## 3. Materialized public document and revision policy

Create the smallest credible schema (normally `site_yearbooks` + `site_yearbook_revisions` + compact coverage table as §4, not an entire telemetry CMS). Model/unique keys by `(site_id, year)` and immutable `revision`. **New tables must have NO foreign keys and NO cascade actions**. Preserve the stable Site UUID, Public ID and archived source identity in annual snapshots, so later removal/archival cannot destroy long-lived evidence. Check entity existence in the bounded transaction with explicit locking when generation runs.

- `site_yearbooks`: site_id, year, public identity copied at first generation, status `draft|published|hidden`, current published revision/digest, published/updated time, algorithm/evidence schema version. Keep any new statuses minimal.
- `site_yearbook_revisions`: identity, year, sequential logical version (revision counter is not an entity primary key), deterministic normalized annual content object (typed, capped), payload digest, generation provenance, generated time, immutable published snapshots. Avoid duplicating all underlying evidence rows inside each snapshot.
- A published revision is **never rewritten in place**. Regeneration with identical semantic digest is a no-op. Genuine correction appends a revision; explicit reviewed publication atomically selects the new revision and retains prior published version for audit. Automatic first publication may happen for qualifying safe historical years; automatic re-publication of an existing annual report is **not** allowed on data drift without review.
- Manual CLI: `yearbook preview <site-public-id> <year>` and `yearbook reconcile [--year YYYY] [--dry-run|--apply]` or equivalent simple Go Cobra commands using the repository's existing explicit YAML. No admin token/client introduced just for this stage; no arbitrary public mutation endpoint. Preview reports facts and eligibility reasons, no unpublished public URL or secret dumping.
- Automatic reconcile: optional `yearbook.enabled` explicit YAML (dev default disabled), bounded **daily** check within the existing GoFurry API runtime owner with PostgreSQL advisory/row locking, no independent service/Redis queue. Only years whose grace period has elapsed; restart and two concurrent API processes cannot duplicate annual publications or revisions. The job must not postpone Fiber readiness or block Start/Wallpaper; failure is bounded and reported with sanitized code, and next schedule retries safely. Operators explicitly enable it in an authorized deployment after reviewing configuration.
- Input to generator: GoFurry's own `site_evidence_changes` and coverage summaries (plus current editorial metadata clearly labeled as generated-at naming if historical names were not recorded). **Never query Harvest during yearbook generation, SSR, or historical correction**.

### Public structure (deterministic bilingual data-driven sections)

- Year and Site identity with canonical published name (including current name vs year-end distinction), optional official primary URL appropriately time-labeled.
- Period summary, recorded dates, unique confirmed days, coverage scope and gaps (Unknown means unknown, not down).
- Verified technology/hosting/platform evolution with confidence, provenance and observed date.
- Material domain/redirect and DNS/TLS certificate changes; show meaningful sanitized subsets, not all raw TXT/MX or full cert/HTML.
- Chronological material-change timeline with type, first-observed date, source, evidence code and detector version. Limit rendered timeline (candidate maximum 40 material entries) with truncation disclosure rather than silently losing data.
- Year-end last-known-good facts with recorded-at, source and uncertainty.
- A short explicit "About these observations" explanation in both languages, plus durable evidence references meaningful after Harvest's 14/30-day retention.
- **No fabricated interpretation**. `zh/en` copy is fixed, versioned templates; free-form translations are not generated from untrusted scraped metadata.

Store a small, bounded JSON document (initial candidate <=64 KiB/version, <=40 summarized timeline entries, max 2 languages); audit actual allocations. Sanitize URL/HTML/plaintext fields, accept only known fact keys and provenance identifiers. Public DTOs exclude raw internal UUID, Harvest keys, private admin/binding state, credentials and sensitive DNS/RDAP content.

## 4. Compact the existing B1 daily coverage

B1's `site_daily_coverage` creates rows by (Site, source, capability, scope, UTC day). Its fixture measured **~262 KB per Site-year** for one confirmed daily scope plus four changes. Yearbook must not reproduce a second year-long daily table.

Build a **monthly compact coverage rollup** (one identity per site, historical binding/source, capability, schema and scope, UTC month) with:
- calendar month, **31-bit validated UTC-day presence mask stored in bigint** (bit 0 for day 1 through bit 30 for day 31), optional small provenance/ruleset/checksum and observed end; OR merge is monotonic;
- each set bit means **there was supporting verified confirmation on that date**; absent bits remain **unknown/unrecorded**, never down;
- yearbook computes **union across scopes and sources per Site per year** when counting distinct days (no double count). Attribution remains anchored to original binding; domain moves do not rewrite older month's identity.
- Keep recent raw daily rows (candidate last 45 days). At month closure, incrementally roll up eligible days. Only after a durable rollup and an exact day-set equivalence check in one safe transactional sequence may the corresponding old daily rows be pruned in bounded batches. The rollup is sufficient to reconstruct which days had evidence; it does not pretend to preserve every per-day receipt timestamp once compacted. Keep all material fact events/provenance forever subject to a separately reviewed retention policy.
- Repeated runs, partial batches, process crash between OR and delete, new late confirmation, snapshot reset and replay expiry **must not lose any coverage**. Do not compact a month that may still receive observations without a defined late-data merge rule. A late verified confirmation updates OR safely but cannot invent missed dates during a 410 gap.
- For reproducibility, retain enough bounded source/window attribution and revisioned cutoff markers that an old annual artifact can be recomputed from fact events and monthly masks.
- If the existing `site_daily_coverage` is already large, backfill in bounded incremental batches, no full-table lock and no destructive one-shot rewrite.
- Measure storage for 100 and 1000 representative Site-years and several scopes per Site. Report table/index/WAL and % savings versus B1 fixture under comparable inputs; if a test fixture differs, label it. No unbounded retention of parallel daily+monthly+annual snapshots.

## 5. Foreign key / cascade audit and forward-only simplification

**User preference:** Do not add foreign keys or cascading deletes unless the constrained parent-child relationship has a clearly documented, compelling long-term correctness value. This is not permission to delete existing data or remove all integrity checks blindly.

- Read D1-A `202611110001_site_game_identity.sql` and D1-B1 `202611110002_harvest_evidence.sql`. B1 introduced substantial FKs: `collection_bindings` to Site/Game/source/address/platform, `collection_plans` to source, `collection_plan_bindings` composite FKs, `collection_gaps/current` and `site_evidence_changes/site_daily_coverage` to mutable tables. **No `ON DELETE CASCADE` appeared in these audited B1 constraints**, but long-lived history tied by FK to mutable operational rows can impede future maintenance.
- **For B2 new yearbook/rollup tables: NO FK, NO ON DELETE CASCADE/SET NULL.** Use immutable UUID identity, unique/check constraints, source-provenance copies and reviewed transaction-level consistency.
- In this same stage, make a focused, **forward-only migration** removing B1 **cross-module/historical-data FKs** that are not essential, especially `site_evidence_changes` and `site_daily_coverage` ownership/binding refs, and `collection_current` refs to operational source that can be retired. Replace FK assumptions with read/insert-time typed ownership checks, deterministic close/archive behavior, unique indexes, and a read-only orphan-integrity audit test/task.
- For D1-A's tight intra-aggregate `site_localizations/site_addresses -> sites` and `game_localizations/game_sources -> games`, keep a FK **only if** it has proven high integrity value that a simpler transaction invariant cannot reliably replace; document why. If there is no compelling case, propose a scoped safe forward migration rather than casually dropping all FKs. Absolutely **no cascaded hard deletion** of Site/Game identities, bound sources, fact history or published yearbooks.
- Do NOT modify historical migration files 0001/0002; apply additive/constraint-altering **Goose forward migration only**. Keep sqlc queries generated and tested. Pre/post migration counts and referenced rows must match; test archive, remove link, prune, reader snapshot and yearbook after deletions. Don't create a new generic ORM cascade or trigger storm.

## 6. Public API/SSR and Start isolation

Public read endpoints under GoFurry's regional API (adapt exact path to existing conventions):
- `GET /api/v1/sites/:publicID/yearbooks` -> published-year summary list, current/allowed visibility only.
- `GET /api/v1/sites/:publicID/yearbooks/:year` -> typed published Yearbook snapshot with required localized sections and evidence; 404 if not eligible/not published/hidden, 503 if GoFurry DB unavailable. No Harvest network call. Do not accidentally expose internal draft/provenance JSON beyond public allowlist.

Frontend route **exactly** `/sites/{public_id}/{slug}/yearbook/{year}` using TanStack Start and optional `/en` (CN) or `/zh` (INTL) prefix. Ensure the optional-slug Site detail route does **not** intercept the Yearbook path as a prefix. Preserve typed `public_id` lookup and canonical slug redirects with 301 and locale, bounded year validation and internal URL builder (no open redirect). Structured 200/301/404/503 responses, accurate title/description, canonical and only actually published translated alternate hreflang. No invented English/Chinese summary or locale fallback in metadata.

**Site detail integration:** add a single small `Yearbooks / 年鉴` link/list of published years in the existing Site detail component (same public ID), not a new observation dashboard. It is only visible if a qualifying public Yearbook exists. Avoid an extra blocking API call on Game routes; query it only for Site and keep current detail behavior on yearbook API failure.

**Start is a protected surface.** Do not edit `apps/web/src/start/**`, Start routes, quick access, settings, theme or wallpaper controls, shared semantic tokens, global SCSS, `__root.tsx`, Preferences, search/weather modules, or core layout to accommodate Yearbook. Put Yearbook code/styles in dedicated `apps/web/src/yearbook/**` and one narrowly scoped Site detail entry. Use the existing visual tokens via local SCSS Modules, accessible typography, restrained layout, responsive dark/light and reduced motion. No new UI library, icon package, CSS runtime, Motion global animation or huge graphical components.

Before and after the stage, run existing Start check suites and compare actual behavior in both locales, light/dark, desktop/mobile, keyboard navigation and reduced-motion. Any failure must be diagnosed; do not update Golden snapshots merely to conceal a Yearbook regression. If an upstream route change is strictly unavoidable, isolate and prove it does not alter Start layout, interaction or SSR.

**Do not treat the current default root cache header and Start privacy settings as a model for public indexable Yearbooks:** route-level appropriate cache/SEO, no authenticated data and no cookie-dependent static content.

## 7. Tests / comprehensive acceptance

Use a separate disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 database and deterministic fixtures. No shared persistent Tailnet dev DB reset, no production keys, no live Harvest crawl; Harvest can be OFF for all Yearbook generation/SSR tests.

1. **Date semantics:** 2026 not published in Nov 2026; 2026 eligible Jan 8 2027 UTC; leap-year/month length/UTC boundary correct; same year 2 tasks+restart produces one annual identity/revision; partial year November first collected is accurately partial.
2. Eligibility: one sample, 13 distinct days, 14 days with insufficient span, 14 days spanning >=28, duplicate scopes/day, conflicting source/tombstones, missing baseline, no evidence: correct published/draft/insufficient outcomes with explicit explanations.
3. Content: site name/slug change, multiple domain moves, data not in current Harvest history, ruleset upgrade does not synthesize migration, DNS TTL changes ignored, TLS certificate fingerprint changes meaningful, missing observations Unknown, never infer uptime. Trust evidence after original Harvest data pruned.
4. Compact storage: one month with repeated multiple scopes/days, gaps, late confirmations, leap February, crash/retry between rollup and delete, 410 reset and repeated migration. Before/after precise day sets match and no double counting. Yearbook regenerated after daily rows pruned remains semantically identical.
5. Schema: no FK/cascade in new B2 tables, reviewed B1 constraints trimmed with proof, D1-A editorial tables safe, external identities and current facts preserved, sqlc generated from committed queries, forward Goose on existing D1-B1 fixture, no production migration.
6. Revision, correction and publication: identical digest no new revision; changed evidence doesn't silently rewrite published annual; explicit reviewed publication appends/selects revised content; visibility withdrawal doesn't destroy historical revision; no unauthorized public writers.
7. API/SSR: CN default zh, INTL default en, alternate prefixes, canonical/hreflang, Site rename 301, invalid/hidden/draft/no-record 404, DB outage 503, Harvest offline still public 200. Site detail Yearbook link only when published, no Game-route yearbook calls.
8. Start isolation: full Start, wallpapers, weather, suggestions, quick-access, settings and visual regressions remain green; no modifications to protected files; route matching does not alter Start, '/' or Game. Confirm keyboard, responsive, light/dark, reduced-motion and metadata.
9. Resource cost: benchmark 100/1000 Site-years with one/multiple scopes and realistic change counts, SQL/WAL/table/index/heap, generator CPU, read latency and idle overhead; report actual observed numbers and upper bounds. Run `task check:api`, `task sql:check`, Go race/integration, catalog tests, existing Start Web/Browser/HMR, `task check:docker`, `task check:containers`, and require matching successful GitHub Actions before phase is accepted.
10. Full operational flow from `yearbook.enabled` (dev-off) through annual UTC timer, preview, eligible automatic publication, Site detail link, public snapshot URL, safe amendment, restart, no duplicates and no additional required always-on process. No public source request required.

## 8. Delivery / stop point

One complete Codex implementation in **librecosta/gofurry develop**. Deliver `docs/v0.1-d1-b2-acceptance.md` with real executed test results, algorithm/version/threshold and source attribution, annual date example, storage comparison, any deliberately retained FK rationale, CI run link, known limits and SHA. Update current `docs/v0.1-d1-b-harvest-evidence-yearbook.md` only with a short superseding note if needed; do not rewrite B1 history or promise beyond actual implementation. Do not create a separate Yearbook microservice or GitHub release. No new app install, email outreach, public release or real 2026 annual document before it closes.

After D1-B2 accept **STOP yearly/observation feature development**. Planned priority:
1. **D2 — Site & Navigation Catalog:** site groups/taxonomy, curated official icons, lists/filtering/search, complete Site detail and SEO, practical management needs.
2. **D3 — Game Catalog:** tags/genres, source rendering, Steam details/prices/media/news/players, game lists/search/collections and SEO, without multi-platform providers prematurely.
3. **D4 — LibreCosta Admin integration:** official Site/Game editing, classification, publication, binding/collection status and audited management actions. No direct Admin access to GoFurry/Harvest DB.
4. **D5 — Legacy GoFurry import:** audited GFN/GFG source export and migration, identity/old-ID redirect mapping, assets, category and game identities, per-region content validation; never port legacy collector/metrics stack.
5. **D6 — CN/INTL publication projection:** region-local DB and identities, approved public content-only Sync, localization, separation of user data and moderation/region constraints.
6. **D7 — Beta publication & quality closure:** indexable SSR/routes, sitemap, canonical, search UX, load/performance and 4C8G deployment/resource verification, R2/Nginx/filing as applicable, backups, security and public UX regression.
Tech Weekly, site-owner outreach, automated newsletters, new Harvest providers, monetization and future user contributions are **post-launch options**, not prerequisites.
